newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Jan-Feb current account gap at $4.6 bln.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Jan-Feb current account gap at $4.6 bln.

text.p: Brazil's current account deficit for January and February stood at $4.584 billion, up from $1.926 billion for the same period last year, the central bank said.
It said the current account balance of payments was $2.683 billion in February 1997, up from $1.901 billion in January this year.
The bank said the current account gap for the 12 months ending in February was equivalent to 3.55 percent of gross domestic product.
The Central Bank said net foreign direct investment in the first two months of the year totaled $1.233 billion after inflows of $285 million in February.
In the first two months of 1996, foreign direct investment was $768 million.

It said the bank's net foreign reserves ended February 1997 at $58.524 billion against $57.806 billion at end-January. According to the international liquidity concept, which includes accounts receivable, net foreign reserves ended February at $59.405 billion against $58.951 billion in January.
The Central Bank said the current account gap of nearly $4.6 billion for the first two months of the year was basically due to the $2.0 billion trade deficit recorded in January and February.

It said the current account was also influenced by net costs on the services account, reflecting repatriation abroad of dividends and profits ahead of the introduciton of the new CPMF financial transaction tax.
The bank said that in the 12 months ending February, Brazil's external financing needs were equivalent to 2.25 percent of GDP, compared with 1.99 percent in the same period a year ago.
